sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Adya Prasad Tewari,Shahnawaz Khan Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and perused the record.

By means of this second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Inayat, who is involved in Case Crime No. 103 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, police station Kothibhar, district Maharajganj, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected vide order dated 20.12.2021 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 54533 of 2019.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 54533 of 2019
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: In this case, the first information report was lodged on 07.05.2019 for the alleged offence under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act against the present applicant Inayat, who is husband of the deceased and his other family members.

1

Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that before the trial Court,
informant Sabibunnisan, who is mother of the deceased, and Abdul Majeed, who is father of the deceased, have been examined before the trial Court as PW-1 and PW-2 on 13.10.2021 and 24.11.2021, respectively, but at the request of prosecution, they have been declared hostile,
therefore, there is bleak chance of conviction of the applicant, who is languishing in jail since 10.06.2019.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the first information report was lodged on 07.05.2019 and statement of prosecution witnesses have been recorded on 13.10.2021 and 24.11.2021, therefore, there is every possibility of winning over the prosecution witnesses from the side of the accused.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that two prosecution witnesses have been examined upto 24.11.2021, therefore, there is every likelihood that during this period, other prosecution witnesses must have been examined.
Since the trial of the applicant is proceeding, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

However, the trial Court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial expeditiously without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
Order Date :- 23.3.2023 Shubham  Inayat vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176387562/
